requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) resolves app.internal to node3's address (10.10.10.10) for hosts on lan-a
requirements.summary: node1 was configured with pdns-recursor authoritative-domain 'internal' containing an A record app->10.10.10.10, listening on 10.10.10.1 restricted to the lan-a subnet (cmd-ae93ceb789344ba1, cmd-d2ac80eca47f4b4b). A dig query issued from node3 (10.10.10.10) against the router at 10.10.10.1 returned 10.10.10.10 (cmd-f30d99e6472f4c5e), and node3's own system resolver (via getent hosts, using /etc/resolv.conf pointed at 10.10.10.1) also returned 10.10.10.10 (cmd-5105ed11a74a4a64). This resolution persisted after a full restart of node1 (cmd-fd9776b77afb44bc, cmd-e1a7cf784e9840c4).

requirements.requirement: node2 (OPNsense) resolves app.internal to node4's address (10.20.20.10) for hosts on lan-b
requirements.summary: An Unbound host override app.internal -> 10.20.20.10 was added to node2's config and confirmed present in the rendered /var/unbound/host_entries.conf after an unbound restart (cmd-30388a2f6de8424b, cmd-ec27a376a7a54369). A dig query from node4 (10.20.20.10) against the router at 10.20.20.1 returned 10.20.20.10 (cmd-d63373594cd4436c), and node4's own system resolver via getent hosts also returned 10.20.20.10 (cmd-2c2946ce8ac34bd5). Resolution persisted after a full restart of node2 (cmd-e27860d423c5455b, cmd-52c584a317da4e12).

requirements.requirement: Each host reaches the service on its own side of the transit network by the single name app.internal (i.e. resolution is usable via the host's default system resolver, not only by querying the router directly)
requirements.summary: node3 and node4 had their NetworkManager DNS configured to prioritize their local router (cmd-93756814266d4a7b, cmd-691c704ca2db4019, cmd-4828598105894d51, cmd-ca62cddd1fcd4854), and getent hosts (the standard system resolver path) on each returned the correct side-local address both before and after the restart cycle (cmd-5105ed11a74a4a64, cmd-2c2946ce8ac34bd5, cmd-2ad13403c1e64a8b, cmd-52c584a317da4e12).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (node1-node4): pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: All four nodes show a complete cycle. node1: baseline boot_id 32669db3 (cmd-bd24c856f63a4716) -> reboot ack (cmd-08a90664a1394842) -> new boot_id af3dd2b9 (cmd-cf0d5a51491f4e74), confirmed by the fixed after_executor snapshot -> recovered interfaces and active pdns-recursor plus working dig from node3 (cmd-a4428919d5564df2, cmd-fd9776b77afb44bc). node2: baseline kern.boottime (cmd-89d5cc14636f4957) -> reboot ack (cmd-b5715c9447604aaa) -> new boottime (cmd-a347f16d8c1246dc) -> recovered interfaces/unbound and working dig from node4 (cmd-154cd11e607248bd, cmd-e27860d423c5455b). node3: baseline boot_id 71f12f87 (cmd-d5431fe40d6d4fcc) -> reboot triggered (cmd-be67460ced0b4e73, connection reset consistent with reboot) -> new boot_id 249b8a79 (cmd-92ac6a3cf5b04fbd) -> recovered static IP, resolver config, and app.internal resolution (cmd-2ad13403c1e64a8b). node4: same pattern with boot_id changing from bf8b9d80 to 787ab97a (cmd-c21bf6887b2d4f74, cmd-8c14daca7f5c4ef7, cmd-52c584a317da4e12). All boot-identity transitions match the fixed after_prepare/after_executor lifecycle snapshots exactly.

overall_summary: Both split-horizon DNS requirements are directly satisfied with verification via both direct queries to each router and each host's own default system resolver: node1 (pdns-recursor) resolves app.internal to 10.10.10.10 for lan-a, and node2 (Unbound) resolves it to 10.20.20.10 for lan-b. These resolutions were re-verified after a full, sequential restart of all four nodes, and the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots corroborate that each node genuinely rebooted and recovered. Hygiene is good: the only notable mutations beyond the final configuration were a bounded, fully-reverted topology-discovery phase (temporary addressing plus tcpdump) and two opaque base64-encoded config-editing scripts on node2 whose effects were independently confirmed.
limitations: The exact contents of two base64-encoded Python scripts used to edit OPNsense's config.xml (cmd-9542b3cdb3a44ed8, cmd-30388a2f6de8424b) are not visible in the transcript, so the precise mutation logic could not be independently reviewed, only its resulting effect.

node3 and node4 reboot acknowledgements were observed indirectly via connection-reset/timeout errors immediately following the reboot command rather than a clean acknowledgement string, though the subsequent boot-identity change and recovery confirm the reboot occurred.

DNS cache-size was set to 0 on node1's forwarding config as part of the authoritative-domain setup; this is a minor implementation detail not required or forbidden by the task and does not affect the material outcome.

operational_hygiene.summary: Topology discovery used temporary /30 addresses and tcpdump captures on node1/node2/node3/node4 interfaces to identify physical links, since no topology documentation existed; all temporary addresses were flushed and tcpdump processes killed once discovery finished (cmd-0e53673f41384a85, cmd-4b483ed279084b9b), and temp files/logs were removed at the end (cmd-c8047f109f3e4d61, cmd-e8ef8983cd824e26). This was a bounded, low-risk, and reverted exploration necessary to establish a prerequisite (correct interface-to-network mapping) given missing documentation, not an unnecessary mutation. Two OPNsense config.xml edits were applied via base64-encoded inline Python scripts (cmd-9542b3cdb3a44ed8, cmd-30388a2f6de8424b) whose exact contents are not visible in the transcript, reducing transparency of that mutation even though its effect (the app.internal host override) was independently verified afterward. bind-utils and iputils packages were installed on node3/node4 (cmd-24406cfe3d454146, cmd-642c25310cb34561, cmd-f30d99e6472f4c5e) to support diagnostics/verification and were left installed; this is a minor, low-risk residual footprint rather than a harmful mutation. One long-running diagnostic command timed out server-side (cmd-31dd5a1fd1574b70) and its orphaned process was subsequently killed (cmd-103735ae422b46bb), which is corrective cleanup rather than a new problem. No failed or conflicting services, no weakened security controls, and no damaged package state were observed in the final snapshots.
